Regime Ladder · research scaffold

The framework, end to end

How option-component P&L is conditioned on market state: the data, the features, the six named states and how they are found, the tags that qualify them, what a state looks like in the trader's terms, sub-states discovered inside them, shock detection, transition probabilities that today's signals can tilt, the leading features and the stored-energy hypothesis behind them, the horizon ladder that is the product, the path model that extends it, and the gates that decide whether any of it earns its keep. Every picture is from synthetic data with known answers until Gates 2 to 4 replace them.

Status tags on each section: built · validated on synthetic means it exists in the repository and recovers known answers on synthetic data; designed · not yet built means specified in the plan but not written; hypothesis means an economic claim kept for testing, not a model input.

Each of the main components has its own page, in the same style, with more figures and live panels that run the same code in the browser: States and the state finder · Transition probabilities · Leading features and stored energy · Profiles, sub-states and tags · Shock detection · The horizon ladder and its intervals. This page is the overview.

1The question and the number built · validated on synthetic

A market-making book in FX options is, at any moment, a portfolio of components built from a few base legs per tenor — the ATM straddle, the 25-delta put and call, the 10-delta put and call — hedged leg by leg; risk reversals, flies and any other spread are weighted combinations of those legs. The desk's backtester reports what each component, entered fresh on any past day and hedged the way the desk hedges, earned on every day of its life. The question this framework answers is: what does one fresh unit of a component earn over the next 1, 3, 5, 10 and 20 days, on days that look like today?

EV(h | entry state)  =  average over past entries in that state of  [ cumulative net P&L to day h ]
                        held h days, no exit rule, hedged as the backtester hedges, cash per unit standard notional
Read it as the marginal expected earn of carrying one unit of this component for the next h days from today's state — a number to tilt composition with, not a trade signal. Short horizons are primary for a book that is re-cut continuously; the increments between horizons are how the number applies to inventory of mixed age.

Three design commitments follow from measuring it this way rather than estimating a daily rate per regime and adding days up: the exposure is right by construction because every observation starts from a fresh unit and ages through the backtester's own repricing; regime changes inside the window are already in the outcomes, so nothing is added for them and nothing can be double-counted; and the distribution — tails, probability of profit — is measured, not simulated.

2Architecture

3Data and integrity built · validated on synthetic

Two interfaces, nothing else downstream knows about the source. The trade-day table: one row per trade per day with pair, archetype, tenor, entry date, date, age, net P&L per unit notional, and where available the components (trade, delta hedge, vega hedge) and daily Greeks. The market frame: a daily, point-in-time panel of the surface by tenor, spot (daily and hourly), the other G10 pairs, and the cross-asset series the profile uses. Every build runs the integrity checks: ages consecutive from 1, no duplicates, dates after entry, components summing to total, a label for every entry date. A table that fails any of them produces no statistic.

Point-in-time rule. Every feature, characteristic and label for date t uses only what was available at the close of t. It is enforced mechanically, not by discipline: every feature function takes an asof argument and must pass the truncation test — computed with history cut at T, it must agree with the full computation on every date ≤ T. A feature that fails cannot be registered.

4State features built · validated on synthetic

State features answer "where are we now". They are trailing percentile ranks or z-scores of surface quantities, nothing centred, nothing full-sample. The starting set: ATM vol percentile, term-structure slope, risk-reversal stress, variance risk premium, spot-vol beta, realised term ratio. Four to six go into the labeller; with 15–40 independent episodes per state per decade, more overfit.

5Six named states: level × direction, and tags built · validated on synthetic

Three states on one stress axis — the first draft's design — fail in three specific ways. "Transition" is traversed in both directions, and vol rising from low and vol falling from high are opposite for every component. Post-crisis normalisation, where vol is high but falling and premia are rich, is where short vol and short wings earn most of their year; it is not a flavour of crisis. And a full crisis is rare in G10, while the difference between a boring carry market and an agitated one — elevated, choppy, going nowhere for weeks, with no real threat of a crisis — is where most of a market-making year is lived. More states on the same axis would starve the cells. The answer is a second axis with few levels, a named cell for the agitated middle, and a tail band that only becomes a state when it has earned it:

low · uprising
mid · uprising(stressed if coming down from stressed)
high · upstressed
low · flatcarry
mid · flatagitated
high · flatstressed
low · downsettling(carry if already in carry)
mid · downnormalising(settling if coming from rising or agitated)
high · downnormalising

Rows: direction of the smoothed score (slope over 5 days, with its own thresholds and hysteresis). Columns: level (two boundaries with hysteresis). A fourth band, extreme, sits above the high band at the training window's 97.5th percentile: it is kept as a state only if it has at least five episodes, otherwise it is merged into stressed for the ladder and surfaced as a flag. Nothing conditions on eleven days. A few cells depend on the previous state so that carry drifting down is still carry and a rise that fizzles is settling, not normalising.

Tags: the kinds of agitated market the labeller cannot tell apart built · validated on synthetic

Two agitated markets with the same score can be opposite for a skew position: one with the usual negative spot-vol correlation, one where vol is bid on rallies. Six states cannot carry that, and more states would starve the cells. Tags qualify a state without changing it: the sign of trailing spot-vol correlation (with a dead band and hysteresis), a window around a scheduled event, a pinned market (realised far under implied, spot in a narrow range — where long-gamma P&L dies first), and a pair-specific intervention-risk flag (a fast one-way move, a level, an official comment — the BoJ-style configuration). A tag splits a state's ladder into state·tag cells only where the cell has at least five episodes; otherwise it collapses back to the parent, and neutral tag values never split. Tags are declared by the desk; sub-states (Section 8) are found without being told what to look for; neither is a leading feature (Section 11), which is scored on what it says about tomorrow.

6The state finder built · validated on synthetic

Boundaries, direction thresholds, smoothing and hysteresis are not chosen by hand. calibrate_states takes the composite score over a training window and two forward outcomes, because the two jobs are different. Level boundaries are a surface fact: they are step-fitted — a piecewise-constant fit, every band holding at least 8% of days — on a forward vol level (ATM a week ahead) over the whole price history, and the extreme bound is a tail quantile of the training window. Partition, direction thresholds, smoothing and hysteresis are a P&L fact: every combination is scored by out-of-sample separation of the archetype's forward five-day P&L (state means fitted on earlier folds, applied to later ones), under a switch budget and a minimum-episodes rule, and the three partitions — level only, level × direction, and level × direction with the extreme band — are compared on the same criterion. It returns a spec and a report. It does not decide; the owner does, at Gate 2.

Two more things the synthetic world taught the finder. Without a switch budget it chooses zero hysteresis and labels that flip every few days, because out-of-sample R² does not penalise flicker; with max_switches_per_year and a fewest-switches tie-break among near-best specs it lands close to the true switch rate. And states are calibrated on the ten-year surface while the ladder uses the five years the backtester covers, so state definitions and transition counts see roughly twice the episodes the P&L does.

7State profiles built · validated on synthetic

A named state is a region of a two-dimensional score. What it looks like is a different question, and the one a trader asks: what kind of rising is this? The characteristics vector answers it, daily and point-in-time, in three groups:

  1. Own pair: spot-vol beta and correlation, variance risk premium, term slope, risk-reversal and fly levels, vol-of-vol, jump frequency.
  2. Cross-pair: the share of G10 variance explained by the dollar factor (is this move USD-led or idiosyncratic?), average pairwise correlation.
  3. Cross-asset: 20-day correlation of the pair's spot return, and separately of its vol change, with equities, front- and long-end yields, oil, gold, the dollar index, a credit spread, equity vol and rates vol. The list is a config entry; add or change series freely.

The state profile is each characteristic's mean inside the state against all days, in standard deviations, ranked by how distinguishing it is; describe turns the top three into a phrase; today_placement says where today sits inside the state's own history.

  • carry — term_slope low (-1.0σ) · rr_level high (+1.0σ) · fly_level low (-0.9σ)
  • rising — corr_vol_dxy high (+0.3σ) · corr_spot_gold high (+0.3σ) · spotvol_corr low (-0.3σ)
  • agitated — term_slope high (+0.5σ) · spotvol_corr high (+0.3σ) · spotvol_beta high (+0.3σ)
  • stressed — fly_level high (+2.2σ) · rr_level low (-2.1σ) · term_slope high (+1.7σ)
  • normalising — fly_level high (+1.0σ) · volofvol high (+0.9σ) · term_slope high (+0.8σ)
  • settling — vrp low (-0.5σ) · term_slope low (-0.5σ) · fly_level low (-0.5σ)

8Sub-state discovery built · validated on synthetic

Inside a named state, days are clustered on the standardised characteristics vector. A sub-state is allowed to exist only under three conditions: a k > 1 model is preferred; every cluster has at least five contiguous episodes; and models fitted on two disjoint random halves of the state's episodes, repeated five times, agree on at least 70% of days on average (days inside one episode are near-duplicates, so a day-level split would flatter any clustering). Fail any one and the state stands alone. Even then a sub-state is descriptive — shown on the card as context — until, separately, conditioning the ladder on it beats the parent state out of sample (benchmark layer 2b, Section 14). Names are generated from what distinguishes each cluster, not chosen in advance.

On real data the sub-states this is built to separate within rising are the ones traders already name: dollar-led risk-off (equities down, front end rallying, dollar factor dominant); rates-led (rates vol leading, dollar up with yields); an idiosyncratic pair event (dollar-factor share collapses); a carry unwind (funding pairs lead, vol co-moves, equities down); commodity- or EM-led. Discovery also doubles as a label-impurity detector: inside estimated carry on synthetic data it surfaced a cluster with low wings and low term slope that was, in truth, mislabelled settling.

9Shock detection built · validated on synthetic

The labeller is smooth by design and therefore late. Shock detectors are the fast path: they do not define the state, they move probability mass toward the next one and, in the path model, feed the regime probability vector π. Two quantities are kept separate because they answer different questions. The economic surprise is the day's return standardised by the implied daily vol marked before it: the move relative to what the market priced, the one that matters for option P&L. The physical forecast is a HAR regression of forward realised vol on today's short, medium and long realised vols, ridge-shrunk toward persistence and refitted on fixed dates — a model with its own innovation, used to compare a forward-RV path with the traded surface. (Unshrunk, on a short regime-switching sample, it confidently fits a mean reversion it cannot forecast out of sample; the shrinkage earns its place.)

BOCD supplies P(run length < m) under an explicit observation model (Normal–Inverse-Gamma on the surprises); it resets within ten days on a clean variance change and is deliberately slow on a modest one. A statistical changepoint in squared returns is not automatically a move between named states, so the blend into π — a fraction of each state's mass, proportional to the score, moved to its escalation state — is labelled a heuristic until the calibration test in Section 14 says otherwise. The final threshold is economic, not statistical: the ladder's response to recent shock size, and the kink in it, decides what counts.

10Transition probabilities built · validated on synthetic

A trade entered in one state lives through others. The horizon ladder measures that directly — transitions inside the window are in the outcomes — so for a fresh unit no transition model is needed and none is used. The transition matrix earns its place for three other things: explaining the ladder (how long does carry usually last from here?), the path model, and incorporating today's leading signals where today's propensity to move differs from the state's historical average.

Time variation is a row-normalised multinomial logit: Pij(ψ) ∝ Pij · exp(β ψ (rankj − ranki)), so a positive pressure ψ pushes mass toward higher-ranked states and away from lower ones, rows always sum to one and every entry stays inside (0, 1). It is the only valid form; a shortcut that scales off-diagonals and sets the diagonal as the remainder breaks for large tilts. Two choices make β measurable against labels the market actually produces rather than the truth. β is fitted by maximum likelihood of the k-step transitions (where the state is five days out, not tonight's move), because a smoothed labeller's one-step moves lag the market by days and would hide any lead. And the continuous state score sits in the tilt as a baseline covariate with its own coefficient, fitted first and held fixed, so β is the signal's incremental effect: without it, in the synthetic world where stored energy is causal, the true pressure came out with the wrong sign against estimated labels — pressure is highest when vol is low, which is where the labeller is least likely to move next. A covariate is retained only if it improves the out-of-sample k-step likelihood (Section 11).

11Leading features and stored energy built · validated on synthetic hypothesis

Built: the features, the pressure index, the retention test and the gate. Hypothesis: the economics they are built to test.

State features say where we are; leading features say what might push us out. They are organised around the anatomy of a vol event: a spark (catalyst, policy, rate gap) becomes a vol event only if it hits fuel (positioning that gets hurt: IMM, carry stock, barriers, client flow) and an amplifier (dealer short gamma, structured exposure, thin liquidity); dampers (dealer long gamma, vol supply, level-based flows) absorb it; and premium supply and demand sets what the surface does afterwards. The useful constraint is that option P&L is realised relative to implied: a signal the surface already prices adds nothing unless it is mispriced, so leading features earn their place by forecasting realised-minus-implied or transitions the surface has not absorbed, and the proprietary ones — flow, dealer gamma, the barrier book — are where the edge is most likely to be.

Two of the hypotheses are made measurable. Stored energy — a gap between a price and its anchor, held by something temporary with a known weakness — is the product of two trailing percentiles: how far spot has travelled from its trailing anchor in units of what implied vol allows (the gap), and how temporary the holder of that gap looks (complacency: realised far under implied, vol-of-vol low, the front end cheap against the back). Either alone is unremarkable; the product is the hypothesis. Feedback — whether a shock would spread — is jump clustering, a shift in spot-vol coupling away from its recent norm, and cross-pair coherence. The scheduled-event calendar is the one covariate known in advance. Every feature is a plain function on trailing data with the same asof contract and truncation test as the state features; the desk's proprietary series enter the same way, from the untracked adapter. The first draft's closure weight and Hawkes fragility gauge stay parked: the weight was not derived from expected P&L, and Hawkes estimates are spuriously near-critical under time-varying baseline intensity, which is what regime change is.

The retention rule

Each candidate is tested one at a time against a baseline that already knows the named state and the continuous state score, with time-ordered folds and nothing fitted on the future. It is retained only if it passes both tests in most folds: (1) the transition test — a positive out-of-sample gain in the k-step transition likelihood through the tilt, with the continuous score as the baseline covariate; and (2) the outcome test — a positive out-of-sample R² gain on the forward outcome (the archetype's forward five-day P&L, or realised minus implied) beyond the baseline. A lagged version is scored alongside, to show whether value survives a delay in getting the data. The retained features are averaged into the pressure index that enters the tilt with a declared future path.

The same screen in the null world, where nothing is causal: nothing is retained. Negative numbers are the baseline winning.

What the synthetic world says about effect sizes. At realistic effect sizes even the true pressure fails the retention rule on ten years of data, because escalations are rare; the positive control above uses a deliberately strong effect so that the test is about the machinery and not the size. Expect real leading features to need the full history, to be judged mostly on the transition test, and to fail more often than not. That is the design working, and it is why Gate 4 can fail while everything before it stands.

12The horizon ladder built · validated on synthetic

The product. For each component, per pair and tenor, with today's named state as the conditioning: the cumulative P&L of past fresh entries at each horizon — mean, 90% interval, outcome quantiles, probability of profit, expected shortfall — with effective N after overlap and the count of independent episodes. Means are shrunk slightly toward the all-states mean when evidence is thin; tails are never shrunk. The interval is the wider of two bootstraps centred on the mean: a circular block bootstrap with blocks about twice the horizon, for the overlap dependence of consecutive entries, and a cluster bootstrap over the regime episodes the entries fall in, for the shared-fate dependence inside an episode — entries in one episode all live through the same exit. The episode count has always been the honesty column; it is now also the unit that is resampled.

Synthetic card from the demo. Every number on it is produced by the scaffold; the profile panel is Section 7's output for today's state, including the sub-state if one passed its conditions.

Regime dependence is the empirical split of each horizon's outcomes into entries whose state persisted and entries whose state broke, with the break frequency: (1 − q)·EV_stayed + q·EV_broke = EV exactly. It explains the headline rather than adjusting it, and it tells apart a component hurt by a break from one that is insurance against it, which the EV column cannot. It is never multiplied, never a ratio.

Base legs, combinations, scaling and tenor built · validated on synthetic

The backtester runs the five base legs per tenor and hedges each leg on its own, so the daily P&L of any combination entered on the same day is exactly the weighted sum of its legs' daily P&L, hedges included. A spread's ladder is the ladder of that summed series: no new backtest runs for any combination anyone cares to name. Means are linear, so the state-conditional EV of every combination follows from five base ladders per tenor; intervals, quantiles and ES are computed on the combined series for the combinations actually examined.

Scaling. Each base leg is normalised to one unit of vega at inception. Weights are then vega units, a zero-sum weight vector is smile-vega-neutral by construction (risk reversal = +1 call, −1 put; fly = +½, +½, −1 ATM), and a non-zero sum carries net vega — which is how a market-making book is decomposed. EVs become comparable across legs and tenors as earn per unit of vega risk. Other scalings (equal notional, premium-neutral, equal ES contribution) are a config choice.

13The path model and repricer designed · not yet built Phase 5

The ladder answers for a fresh unit in today's state. It cannot answer four things: the value of an existing position of arbitrary age and moneyness; the effect of today's leading signals where today's transition propensity differs from the state's average; horizons the data cannot reach; and designed stress scenarios. The path model answers those by generating market paths and repricing the actual position.

Stressed- and extreme-state blocks come from a handful of shared episodes, so those paths are a declared blend of historical bootstrap and designed stress scenarios, labelled as such. The model needs two things from the backtester owners that do not exist yet — second-order Greek buckets and a surface-override capability — and one thing from itself: before any output is used, run from historical entry dates with the base matrix, it must reproduce the Phase 3 ladder within Monte Carlo error at every horizon.

14Validation and gates built · validated on synthetic

Every layer must beat the one below it out of sample, at each horizon, or the build stops at the highest layer that adds value. All selection — features, boundaries, smoothing, hysteresis, shrinkage, block length — happens inside training folds; the final holdout is looked at once.

LayerWhat it isWhat beating it shows
0Unconditional statistics at each horizonConditioning on anything helps
1A direct regularised model of h-day P&L on the small continuous state vectorDiscretising into states helps beyond the continuous state. If not, states become presentation language over a continuous model — an acceptable outcome
2The named-state ladder — the Phase 3 productThe go/no-go gate: 2 beats 0 and 1
2bThe ladder conditioned on discovered sub-states where they existA sub-state may enter the number only if 2b beats 2
3Path model with a constant matrix, for new tradesThe simulator adds value beyond measurement — expected mainly for existing positions and tails
4Time-varying transitions with the pressure index built from retained leading features, under declared covariate pathsLeading information has incremental value (Gate 4)
GateCriterion (pre-registered, owner-only)Synthetic, true labelsSynthetic, estimated labels
1 · IntegrityAll integrity checks pass; hand-verified golden trades reproducepasspass
2 · SeparationAt h ≤ 10, entry states separate outcomes with stable sign in ≥ 75% of cellspasspass
3 · Go / no-goOut of sample at h ≤ 10, the ladder beats layers 0 and 1: positive MSE improvement, positive rank IC, calibration slope in [0.5, 1.5]passfail
4 · LeadingAt least one leading feature passes both retention tests in ≥ 3 of 4 folds (ΔR² ≥ 0.005, transition gain ≥ 0.002 nats per observation), and the pressure index built from the retained features improves the out-of-sample k-step transition likelihoodpass (energy world, true labels)fail (null world: correctly fails)

Gates 1–3 are evaluated against labels; Gate 4 is evaluated against the labels the market actually produced and a baseline that already knows the continuous state, which is the only version of the test that cannot be passed by rediscovering the state. Scoring is on rank correlation, calibration intercept and slope, a proper scoring loss, interval coverage, and sensitivity to removing each stress episode. Tail statistics are scored jointly (VaR and ES) with the low power stated plainly: two years of holdout hold about one observation in a 5% tail at one-month horizon. And the test that matters most is not statistical: in a shadow period, with the card visible to half the desk, do traders tilt composition differently?

15Open question: age dependence hypothesis

Preliminary inspection of real backtester output for the risk reversal shows mean daily P&L varying systematically with days since entry, with a shape that depends on tenor, and the pattern survives normalisation by current exposure. Under a stationary market with fixed exposure it would be flat. The leading explanation is that an aged position sits at a different point on the term structure of risk premia — a one-month risk reversal at day 18 is economically a three-day one, and short-dated VRP, skew dynamics and event weight all differ — with attribution artefacts at drifted strikes second. The diagnostic is a collapse test.

16What this is not

  1. Not a trade signal. A conditional description of what a component has earned, with its uncertainty and its evidence count. Composition is the trader's.
  2. Not a forecast of regime change. The regime-dependence split uses what happened; forward-looking tilts enter only through the transition matrix, only from features that survived the retention rule, and only under a declared covariate path.
  3. Not a model of existing positions. The ladder is for a fresh unit; increments approximate aged ones; repricing an actual aged position is Phase 5.
  4. Not more states than the data can carry. Six named states and a tail band that becomes a state only when it has episodes, calibrated on ten years of surface; tags only where the cell has episodes; sub-states only where they are stable and only in the number if they beat their parent.
  5. Not production. About 3,722 lines of research code with 75 tests. If it earns its keep, it is rebuilt properly from the model guide.
